key_insight: The paper develops a theoretical framework for score-guided probability flows on SE(3), addressing low-density score singularities, space–time regularity, and mean-field game equilibria.
engineering_relevance: The framework could inform stable generative models and multi-agent control for systems combining 3D position and orientation.
method: Control singular score drift using weighted flux dissipation and boundary-preserving Lie-group mollification.
Apply 7D space–time elliptic estimates to analyze regularity.
Use Schauder–Tychonoff fixed points to establish score-guided Nash equilibria.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical bounds and existence results, but no numerical experiments, datasets, or empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The claimed additive spectral-gap boost requires careful verification of metric, domain, and boundary assumptions; positive rotational Ricci curvature alone does not establish it.
paper_title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
